about: Pind Hospitality runs Punjabi-cuisine restaurants under the 'Pind Punjab' brand in Pune, Maharashtra, with most sales coming from delivery through third-party food apps. It has four restaurants on lease (plus one leased by its 97.5%-owned partnership firm) and a food counter, and about 135 employees. It plans a hotel-cum-banquet project in Lonavala.

other.name: Revenue from third-party food delivery apps

objects.purpose: Capex for hotel-cum-banquet hall (Haveli Project) in Lonavala

promoters.background: Nimish (Chairman and MD) and Chirag (WTD) are brothers; Anita is their mother. They manage restaurant roll-out and day-to-day strategy.

concentration.note: Third-party food delivery apps gave Rs 19.16 crore of Rs 24.45 crore FY26 revenue (about 78%). 100% of revenue is from Pune.

litigation_note: Seven tax proceedings against the Company with aggregate amount Rs 1.69 crore (168.69 lakh); further tax proceedings involve the partnership firm and Promoters. No criminal or SEBI actions shown for the Company.
strengths: Established 'Pind Punjab' brand with a hybrid online and offline model; about 4.3 lakh delivery orders a year.
Revenue grew every year, from Rs 20.78 crore in FY24 to Rs 24.45 crore in FY26.
EBITDA margin has stayed in the 15-16% range (16.14% in FY26).
Positive operating cash flow in all three years (Rs 3.05 crore in FY26).
ROCE of 15.83% and RoNW of 15.65% in FY26.
Experienced promoter family actively involved in operations.
Affordable thali-based menu with 200+ dishes across Punjabi, Chinese and Thai cuisine.
Owns the Lonavala land (Rs 6.05 crore) for the planned Haveli project.

risks.title: Heavy reliance on food delivery apps
risks.detail: Delivery apps gave Rs 19.16 crore of Rs 24.45 crore FY26 revenue (about 78%). Loss of or worse terms with these platforms would hit sales hard.

risks.title: All revenue from Pune
risks.detail: 100% of revenue in FY24, FY25 and FY26 came from Pune, so any local disruption hits the whole business.

risks.title: Entire proceeds go to one new project
risks.detail: Rs 12.70 crore of the fresh issue funds the Lonavala Haveli project, estimated at Rs 21.42 crore excluding land. Orders for remaining spend are not yet placed, so cost and time overruns are possible. Project not appraised by any bank.

risks.title: Rising debt and thin liquidity
risks.detail: Borrowings rose to Rs 12.74 crore in FY26 from Rs 8.66 crore, debt/equity about 1.04. Current ratio fell to 0.90 and cash was only Rs 0.01 crore. Promoters are co-borrowers and the Lonavala land is mortgaged.

risks.title: Leased premises
risks.detail: All restaurants operate on leave-and-license terms of 12-60 months. Rent rises or non-renewal could hurt (the Baner outlet closed in FY26 after a lease was not renewed).

risks.title: Tax proceedings
risks.detail: Seven tax proceedings against the Company involve Rs 1.69 crore; the partnership firm and Promoters also face tax cases.

risks.title: Negative investing and financing cash flows
risks.detail: Investing outflow was Rs 6.47 crore in FY26 (mainly Haveli capex) and financing flows were negative in earlier years. Sustained outflows could strain finances.

risks.title: Statutory filing delays
risks.detail: Past delays in GST, EPF and ESIC filings led to late fees and interest. Repeated delays could add costs.

notes: Restated standalone FY24-FY26 figures in Rs lakh converted to Rs crore; the Company also holds a 97.5% share in partnership firm Pind Punjab (not consolidated).
